source.title: On two open problems concerning weak Roman domination in trees

accepted.question_text: Let T be a tree. The weak Roman domination number γr(T) is the minimum weight of a function f: V(T) → {0,1,2} such that every vertex v with f(v)=0 is adjacent to a vertex w with f(w)>0 for which moving one unit from w to v—so that v receives value 1, w is decreased by 1, and all other vertex values stay unchanged—leaves no undefended vertex. The 2-rainbow domination number γr2(T) is the minimum weight of a function g: V(T) → P({1,2}) such that every vertex assigned the empty set sees both colors 1 and 2 in the union of the labels on its neighbors. Characterize all trees T satisfying γr(T)=γr2(T).
accepted.context_brief: Equality of weak Roman and 2-rainbow domination on trees

evidence.quote: Problem 1. Characterize the trees T satisfying γr(T) = γr2(T).
In this paper, we characterize all trees T with γr(T) = γr2(T) or γr(T) = γR(T) answering two open problems posed by Chellali, Haynes and Hedetniemi [Discrete Appl. Math. 178 (2014), 27–32].
Theorem 3.7. Let T be a tree of order n ≥ 3. Then γr(T) = γr2(T) if and only if T ∈ T .

accepted.question_text: Let T be a tree. The weak Roman domination number γr(T) is the minimum weight of a function f: V(T) → {0,1,2} such that every vertex v with f(v)=0 is adjacent to a vertex w with f(w)>0 for which moving one unit from w to v—so that v receives value 1, w is decreased by 1, and all other vertex values stay unchanged—leaves no undefended vertex. The Roman domination number γR(T) is the minimum weight of a function h: V(T) → {0,1,2} such that every vertex assigned 0 is adjacent to some vertex assigned 2. Characterize all trees T satisfying γr(T)=γR(T).
accepted.context_brief: Equality of weak Roman and Roman domination on trees
